facts.content: Patient reports a sudden severe left-sided headache that began at 05:30 today and woke him from sleep.
facts.source_text: CC: Sudden severe L-sided HA since 05:30 today; woke pt from sleep

facts.content: The headache has been constant and worse on waking.
The headache is associated with mild photophobia.
The headache was associated with minimal early dizziness.
The patient reports no nausea or vomiting with the headache.
The patient reports no fever with the headache.
The patient reports no neck stiffness with the headache.
The headache improves after the patient settles when supine.
Paracetamol has been ineffective for the current headache.
The patient has had no prior similar unilateral headaches; past headaches were frontal and milder.
facts.source_text: no prior similar unilateral HA (past HAs frontal, milder)

facts.content: The patient reports increased work stress for two months and late nights as associated factors.
facts.source_text: Triggers/assoc:  work stress 2 mo, late nights

facts.content: Patient has a history of generalized anxiety disorder.
Patient is taking sertraline.
Patient uses paracetamol as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's mother has anxiety.
There is no family history of migraine reported.
Patient lives with a partner.
Patient is a non-smoker.
Patient runs approximately three times per week.
Patient has a cat at home.
Patient has a job with a high workload.
Assessment is acute unilateral headache with possible migraine versus tension-type and no red-flag features reported.
facts.source_text: 1. Acute unilateral HA migraine vs tensiontype, no red-flag features reported

facts.content: Work-related stress and anxiety are considered contributory to the headache and are reported as stable on sertraline.
facts.source_text: 2. Work-related stress/anxiety  stable on sertraline, contributory to HA

facts.content: Plan to start ibuprofen at high dose per migraine guideline and possibly continue paracetamol for headache management.

facts.content: Patient is advised to drink at least 1.5 to 2 liters of water per day and aim for 7 to 8 hours of sleep per night.

facts.content: Plan to provide written headache red-flag advice and advise a low threshold to re-present if symptoms worsen.
facts.source_text: Provide written HA red-flag advice; low threshold to re-present if worse

facts.content: Follow-up by tele-consult is planned in one week with consideration of labs or imaging if there is no improvement.
facts.source_text: F/U tele-consult in 1 wk; consider labs/imaging if no improvement

facts.content: For stress and anxiety, a one-week self-certified sick leave is recommended to reduce workload stress.
facts.source_text: Recommend 1-wk sick leave (self-cert) to reduce workload stress

facts.content: Patient is signposted to a self-referral counseling service link.
Patient is to be educated on warning signs including severe worsening, neurological deficits, persistent vomiting, and visual changes.

facts.content: A tele-consult follow-up is scheduled in one week.
